headline: CALEDONIA DOUBLES DOWN IN ZIMBABWE — Blanket Mine Soars 22% to 2.18Moz @ 3.83 g/t; Maiden Motapa Resource 510,000oz Declared Same Day
snippet: Caledonia Mining (NYSE-A/TSX/VFEX: CMCL) simultaneously announced a 22% jump in Blanket Mine's underground M&I resources to 2.178 million ounces at 3.83 g/t gold — driven by $2.92/oz deep-drill discovery cost — alongside a maiden resource at Motapa of 379,000oz M&I at 1.51 g/t plus 131,000oz Inferred after a $7 million exploration spend. Two resource upgrades on one morning signal a rapidly expanding Zimbabwe gold portfolio at a time when operators need reserve replacement most.

headline: CATL JIANXIAWO RESTART IN DOUBT — Uncertainty Over World's 4th-Largest Lithium Mine Could Fuel Q4 Price Shock
snippet: Analysts warn that fresh uncertainty over the restart of CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine — representing 4–5% of global supply when fully operational — could reignite lithium carbonate price volatility heading into Q4 2026. The mine's stalled restart has already placed a price floor under a market that spent the summer bracing for oversupply; if the restart timeline slips further, the supply-demand calculus swings sharply tighter.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,608 AS WARSH HANGOVER FADES — Miners Recover Despite AEM Dropping 4.18% on Hawkish Macro Read
snippet: Spot gold recovered to $4,608/oz by end of Friday as markets absorbed Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut — a 1.2% intraday drop that briefly rattled the sector. Agnico Eagle fell 4.18% on the day as the stronger dollar pressured gold equities, though the broader metal remains up $1,191 year-over-year and the gold miner index is still on track for the best monthly gain in recorded history.

headline: CYGNUS METALS STRIKES 14.2 g/t AuEq OVER 3.4m — Copper Rand Extension Grades Above Current Resource at Chibougamau, Quebec
snippet: Cygnus Metals (ASX: CY5; TSX-V: CYG) released drilling results at the Copper Rand and Gwillim targets within its Chibougamau Copper-Gold Project in Quebec, highlighted by 20.3 metres at 4.2 g/t gold-equivalent from 399 metres depth — including a high-grade core of 3.4 metres at 14.2 g/t AuEq (2.0 g/t Au, 8.5% Cu, 47.1 g/t Ag). The holes step out 200 metres along strike from historic workings, extending a copper-gold system that remains open.

headline: NEW Cu-Ni-Co ZONE AT BATHURST CAMP — SLAM Drills 67.4m Sulphide Body 2km Outside Logan at Goodwin Project, Assays Pending
snippet: SLAM Exploration (TSX-V: SXL) announced a new massive sulphide discovery from hole GW26-36 at the Goodwin Copper-Nickel-Cobalt Project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp — 2,000 metres northwest of the Logan zone and associated with a newly modelled VTEM geophysical plate. The 67.4-metre sulphide intercept marks the first confirmation of a separate zone; 992 samples across 12 holes are currently at the lab with assays expected within weeks.

headline: BMI LIFTS LITHIUM FORECAST TO $20,100/T — But Warns 2026 Rally Has 'Outrun Fundamentals'; 2027 Surplus On the Way
snippet: Fitch Solutions' BMI unit raised its 2026 average Chinese lithium carbonate forecast to $20,100 per tonne — nearly double last year's $10,502 average — while cautioning that the price recovery has moved faster than supply fundamentals justify. Global lithium production is forecast to grow 13.2% in 2026 led by Australia and China, with previously mothballed operations returning; BMI expects a meaningful surplus to materialise by 2027, making CATL's Jianxiawo restart the single biggest price swing factor in the near term.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER SETS DEERHORN RECORD — 48.5m @ 3.32% Cu Is Longest High-Grade Intercept Ever Drilled at Woodjam, BC
snippet: Vizsla Copper (TSX-V: VCU) reported the longest high-grade copper intersection ever drilled at its Deerhorn deposit on the Woodjam Project in central British Columbia — 48.5 metres grading 3.32% copper, 0.23 g/t gold and 16.59 g/t silver within a broader envelope of 266 metres at 0.97% copper. The result is from drill hole DH26-136 completed during the summer 2026 program; Woodjam hosts multiple copper porphyry deposits and the Deerhorn intercept confirms high-grade continuity at depth.

headline: GOLD FIELDS FCF DOUBLES TO $2.2B IN H1 — Launches $500M Buyback as August Gold Price Lifts Sector Cash Generation to Decade High
snippet: Gold Fields (NYSE: GFI) reported first-half 2026 adjusted free cash flow of $2.225 billion — more than double the year-earlier figure — as the Salares Norte ramp and elevated gold prices drove attributable production 12% higher year-on-year to 1.267 million ounces. The company expanded its existing buyback with a fresh $500 million tranche in August, part of a $1.25 billion total shareholder return program — adding to sector-wide evidence that senior gold producers are now generating more cash than they can deploy in organic growth alone.

headline: BANYAN GOLD OPENS NEW YUKON FRONT — Seattle Creek Hole Confirms Fresh Gold-Silver System 25km from AurMac
snippet: Banyan Gold (TSX-V: BYN) confirmed a new mineralised system at the Seattle Creek zone on its Nitra Project in Yukon — 25 kilometres west of the AurMac Deposit — with the first drill hole returning 1.4 metres at 4.04 g/t gold and a high-grade half-metre of 5.70 g/t Au and 544 g/t Ag near surface. With assays from the lower 500 metres of the 600-metre hole still pending and ten more targets queued for the 2026 drill season on Banyan's 830 sq km land package, this is a genuine greenfield discovery opening.

headline: KAMOA-KAKULA STAGE 2 DEWATERING STARTS — Ivanhoe Holds 2026 Guidance Until Recovery Plan Advances; World's #2 Copper Mine Races to Restart
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines is withholding revised 2026 production guidance at Kamoa-Kakula pending further progress on Stage 2 dewatering of the Kakula Mine — itself now underway as scheduled in August following completion of Stage 1 rehabilitation across 13.4 kilometres of underground workings. The world's second-largest copper mine by grade has been offline or partially curtailed since seismic flooding events in late 2025 forced Ivanhoe to cut its 2026 guidance to 290,000–330,000 tonnes from the original 380,000–420,000 tonne forecast; a successful Stage 2 dewatering would be the key catalyst for a guidance restoration.
